scope: Unilateral-contact plate calculation of every hold-down load corner at 0.7/0.8/0.9 mm finished board thickness, on the native outline and pad positions of the bound PCB. Not a fixture acceptance, not a measured contact/force/stroke result, not a manufacturing release, and not a transfer of the 1.6 mm PASS.

pcb_identity.geometry_revision_note: outline, pads and courtyards come from the native record of this PCB revision, which is the adopted routed 0.8 mm controller. The finished thickness used by the plate model is the ordered 0.8 +/-0.1 mm, which is an order specification, not a measured board.
pcb_identity.rebind_prerequisite: fresh native geometry for the new board bytes first: python3 scripts/a7_fixture_geometry.py --from-zip <native-gate artifact.zip> for a CI-retained artifact, or --from-dir <staged a7-gate root> --expect-revision <checkout SHA> for a run of the pinned image (that record is labelled LOCAL_PINNED_IMAGE_RUN and is not CI-retained evidence); then the command above. --check fails until the record and the board bytes agree

model.plate: Kirchhoff plate, Bogner-Fox-Schmit rectangular C1 elements (tensor cubic Hermite, 4 DOF per node)
model.domain: board rectangle 16.2 x 62.9 mm; holes, copper, component stiffening and the board bow are not modelled
model.contact: node-wise Signorini conditions against the rigid carrier land (w >= 0, reaction >= 0, w * reaction = 0); the land can only push up. No bilateral result is used.
model.solvers: flexibility-form primal active set (scripts/a7_fixture_contact.ContactModel) with an independent stiffness-form active set used as a cross-check; both verify the contact conditions and the equilibrium residual from K u - f after the solve and raise instead of returning a violated state
model.loads: uniform pressure patches: probe tip 0.5 mm diameter (INGUN tip style), clamp pin at the board-contact diameter of each layout (1.5 mm POM thrust pin; 1.2 mm on the stepped tip, see clamp_contact_diameters_mm); total force exact per patch

model.review: method is intended to be re-derived independently: the element matrix, the contact conditions and the mesh study are each checked by scripts/tests/test_a7_fixture_contact.py and scripts/tests/test_a7_fixture_plate.py against closed-form or analytic results

limits.land_lift_limit_basis: PROJECT-CHOICE, same value: how far the board may rise off the carrier land anywhere. alternative_clamp_sites.ranking: planar rules, then the rigid-body net-load-point margin over every force corner of the ranking band, plus the widest clamp y spreads; the shortlisted pairs are solved with the contact model at the governing corner (thinnest board, both plungers at the minimum of their own band, probes at maximum stroke force)
alternative_clamp_sites.shortfall: The current candidate pair meets every recorded load limit at this corner but keeps 0.025 mm worst-case board-edge margin on its second pin, below the 0.15 mm recorded requirement. Of the pairs that satisfy every planar rule, 34 pass rigid statics, and none of the solved ones meets the contact-model limits: the best solved alternative lifts the board 0.422392957 mm off the land against the 0.1 mm limit. The reason is geometric: the planar rules confine every rule-satisfying site to y <= 22.3 mm against a probe field at y [22.4, 28.2], so no admissible pair straddles it and the board tips. Closing the shortfall needs an input this calculation cannot supply: a smaller sourced plunger body, a narrower J5 notch, a larger pressure plate, or an owner decision to accept a smaller edge margin as a gauged incoming-acceptance requirement. This paragraph is about moving full-diameter pins; the adopted candidate instead keeps the sites and reduces the contact diameter of the second pin (see adopted_candidate).
alternative_clamp_sites.status: CALCULATED ALTERNATIVES, NOT ADOPTED: new clamp sites change the pressure-plate taps and need the fixture CAD, manifest identity locks, a sourced plunger and owner review

assumptions: Finished thickness 0.8 +/-0.1 mm is the JLCPCB published tolerance for boards below 1.0 mm (https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/Capabilities, read 2026-11-16 UTC); the ordered specification is not yet placed and no board has been measured.
Flexural modulus 18000 MPa and Poisson ratio 0.3 are ASSUMED; sourced FR-4 class values are recorded for comparison only and do not bound this laminate.
The carrier land is treated as rigid and flat; land flatness, plate stack flatness and pin tip coplanarity are acceptance requirements, not measured values.
Board bow and warp are not modelled (zero initial gap). A bowed board changes the contact set.
Plunger forces follow the catalogue line between F1 and F2 with a +/-20 % acceptance band; the catalogue prints no tolerance, so the band is a PROJECT-CHOICE acceptance requirement.
Probe forces follow the datasheet linear force-stroke line; the value at maximum stroke is read off the graph.
Holes, copper, solder mask and component stiffening are omitted from the plate; omitting copper is not conservative in every direction and remains an open modelling item.
Component heights, solder envelopes and the pressure-plate CAD interference are outside this record.
remaining: Native geometry from a CI-retained artifact: the bound record comes from a gate run in the pinned image on a development machine (no GitHub run id), so re-take it with --from-zip once CI has retained an artifact for these board bytes, then re-run rebind_command.

Physical contact and load validation: measured plunger force at both compression ends, measured probe force, stroke, seating against the datum pins, positioning, and inspection for board damage, with fixture and board unit IDs, instruments and raw data (fixture criterion 5).
Measured finished board thickness and laminate flexural properties of the ordered boards.
Board flatness/bow acceptance and its effect on the contact set.

Fabricator selection and machining capability for the plates and the tapped pin holes.
